doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Deaths and the state of the country
title: The state of the country: corruption, crisis as opportunity, Trump and the pandemic
summary: Asked about the country, Baron calls the system corrupt, criticizes Trump's pandemic leadership, and sees an opportunity for change.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well I don’t mind going to a place in our conversation where — this is not just a conversation about musicians but I’m interested in your general feeling about the state of our country.

Okay. I can tell you that it’s gotten clearer to me. The Japanese — I’ve heard that this may not be true but I heard it so long ago that it was true that I choose to believe it. And the Chinese rather. They have all these symbols for writing the language, and that the symbol for crisis is the same for opportunity, which spiritually speaking makes a lot of sense. I mean the system had gotten so corrupt, let’s face it, it’s gotten extremely corrupt on both sides of the aisle, more on one than the other, more on the right than the left I think but still corrupt. To make a change, to make a — it’s almost like the whole thing had to blow up to make some new grass roots changes and that’s what’s happened, it’s blown up. Every time I see the man in the White House do something really insane, day

by day, I tell myself I shouldn’t be aghast at that because we know what he’s like. I mean so there’s so much stuff, including racism now in addition to just poor leadership about the whole pandemic thing. You know standing there, “Well we’ve got ten cases, it’ll be down to five then nothing in a few days, don’t worry about it.” And then going as far as saying, “Well 100,000 is not bad, we’re doing a great job.” We’re not doing a great job, and people know it. But people also are starting to realize the only way you know when he lies is when he opens his mouth. They used to say that about Bush Senior but it’s more real now. And I’m not afraid to speak these things, and I really believe in spiritual change, and I think individual change makes for changes in the world. And a lot of stuff has hit the fan now. It’s not easy to be in it, some days I’m really upset. But I think it also is the time of opportunity.

Isn’t it interesting, if someone had asked me two weeks ago what kind of incident would replace the newscasters doing it, you know, like here’s the first story of my segment, to replace conversation about the pandemic, I would have thought it would have to be like a nuclear explosion or something. And now we have this racial incident sparked in Minneapolis and wow, it has been story number one.
Yeah. The critical mass has been achieved.
